status: candidate research components; not a validated universal workflow

modules.purpose: Define the variables, eligible evidence, extraction units, missingness conventions and decision rules before comparing extractors.
modules.record: Version the codebook, instructions and prompts; retain training and pilot decisions, held-out evaluation rules and any subsequent amendments.
modules.evaluate: Test whether independent humans, LLMs and supported raters apply the same operational definitions. Separate misunderstanding of a rule from failure to follow a sufficiently specified rule.
modules.question: Which examples, training procedures and rule representations improve extraction without concealing unresolved construct ambiguity?
modules.limit: Instruction compliance and schema completion do not establish that a psychological construct has been operationalized validly.
modules.name: Define variables and coding rules

modules.purpose: Establish which article versions, appendices and other eligible materials enter the extraction, and preserve the information needed downstream.
modules.record: Retain the document inventory, versions and identifiers; the parsing or OCR route; page and table locators; and checks of missing or degraded material.
modules.evaluate: Distinguish document coverage and preservation of layout, digits and reading order from the correctness of later extraction judgments.
modules.question: Where do source acquisition, OCR and representation choices produce omissions or distortions that humans or LLMs can detect or repair?
modules.limit: Document-parsing scores do not establish that all materials for a review were obtained or that review variables were extracted correctly.
modules.name: Prepare and read source documents

modules.purpose: Find the evidence relevant to a variable across text, tables, figures, appendices and dispersed passages.
modules.record: Store the question or query, materials searched, candidate evidence and exact source locations, including relevant information that could not be located.
modules.evaluate: Measure source-evidence recall and precision separately from answer accuracy, using a reference procedure whose coverage is itself documented.
modules.question: Which retrieval strategies reduce missed evidence, and when do additional searches correct errors or introduce distracting candidates?
modules.limit: Long-context and question-answering tasks assess related capabilities; their scores do not establish exhaustive search in psychological studies.
modules.name: Locate relevant evidence

modules.purpose: Associate a candidate value with the correct study, sample, group, outcome, time point and analytical unit.
modules.record: Preserve row and column headers, units, footnotes, relevant sample identifiers and the relationship between each candidate value and its source context.
modules.evaluate: Score correct value–unit assignments and complete records, rather than counting an isolated number as correct when it belongs to the wrong subgroup.
modules.question: Which structured representations and checks help humans and LLMs distinguish overlapping samples, outcomes and repeated measurements?
modules.limit: Table and diagram tasks provide component evidence; transfer to heterogeneous psychological study designs remains to be tested.
modules.name: Bind values to the correct unit

modules.purpose: Translate evidence into the category or value specified by the codebook, retaining defensible alternatives when the source is ambiguous.
modules.record: Link the interpretation to the applicable rule and supporting evidence; record missingness decisions, competing interpretations and confidence or uncertainty separately.
modules.evaluate: Use source-based reference judgments and describe how ambiguity was adjudicated. Report agreement without treating agreement alone as proof of correctness.
modules.question: When do human expertise, LLM interpretation and joint review improve semantic coding, and where do they share the same errors?
modules.limit: Generic annotation and biomedical appraisal studies do not validate the meaning of a psychological review's codebook.
modules.name: Interpret evidence and apply coding rules

modules.purpose: Coordinate retrieval, tool use and dependent operations so intermediate decisions can be inspected and reconsidered.
modules.record: Identify the model snapshot, harness, tools, prompt and instruction versions, available context, budgets and consequential intermediate inputs and outputs.
modules.evaluate: Compare model and harness contributions under matched or explicitly different conditions. Preserve failed and corrected steps as well as the accepted result.
modules.question: Which tool and context arrangements improve extraction, and which apparent gains arise from changes in models, inputs, budgets or supervision?
modules.limit: An agent's success on a research or tool-use task does not establish success on the target extraction workflow.
modules.name: Coordinate retrieval, tools and intermediate steps

modules.purpose: Transform reported inputs into the requested value using explicit formulas, units and executable operations where appropriate.
modules.record: Store input values and locators, the formula and its assumptions, code or tool calls, rounding rules and intermediate and final outputs.
modules.evaluate: Separate retrieval and formula-selection errors from arithmetic or execution errors. Independently check important transformations against the source inputs.
modules.question: Which transformations benefit from deterministic tools, and where do humans or LLMs select an inappropriate formula or set of inputs?
modules.limit: Arithmetic benchmark performance does not validate effect-size formula selection, eligibility decisions or study-specific assumptions.
modules.name: Transform and calculate values

modules.purpose: Check whether a candidate value and its interpretation are supported by the recorded source and extraction rule.
modules.record: Document what was checked, the verifier and information available to that verifier, detected omissions or unsupported additions, and corrections or newly introduced errors.
modules.evaluate: Assess error detection and correction separately, including false reassurance and harmful corrections. Apply comparable reference definitions to human and LLM outputs.
modules.question: When do independent verification, targeted checks or combinations of human and AI verification improve the final extraction?
modules.limit: A complete verification log does not establish that the verifier's judgment is correct or that the reference labels are error-free.
modules.name: Verify source support and detect errors

modules.purpose: Specify how human experts, research assistants and LLMs contribute, and when each sees another actor's output.
modules.record: Retain initial judgments when the design includes independent extraction; otherwise document the timing of AI exposure, revisions, coder expertise and training, time and workload.
modules.evaluate: Compare human-only, LLM-only and human–AI conditions without assuming an accuracy ordering. Measure corrected, retained and introduced errors as well as efficiency and independence.
modules.question: Which allocation and exposure designs combine complementary abilities, and when do deference, fatigue or incomplete search impair each type of workflow?
modules.limit: Human–AI studies in adjacent tasks inform the design of comparisons but do not establish their effects in psychological data extraction.
modules.name: Combine human and LLM contributions

modules.purpose: Resolve discrepancies through source evidence and coding rules, while retaining uncertainty when the available information does not support one defensible answer.
modules.record: Preserve competing values, actor identities or roles, evidence and rules considered, the reason for acceptance or escalation, and unresolved cases.
modules.evaluate: Distinguish agreement, consensus and correctness. Record how the reference was constructed and whether adjudicators were independent of the compared extraction conditions.
modules.question: Which adjudication arrangements identify human and LLM errors rather than merely privileging one actor's initial judgment?
modules.limit: Consensus is not an automatically error-free gold standard, and generic resistance-to-pressure tests do not validate extraction adjudication.
modules.name: Resolve disagreements without yielding to pressure

modules.purpose: Evaluate the resulting review data at the field, relationship and whole-record levels, with omissions and unsupported additions made explicit.
modules.record: Define the eligible denominator, missing-value treatment, reference construction and ambiguity rules, and report accuracy alongside time, cost and actor expertise.
modules.evaluate: Use the same scoring rules and reference definitions across compared conditions; report important subgroups and error types rather than relying solely on a pooled agreement index.
modules.question: Which workflow components improve final data quality, for which variables and source conditions, and at what cost?
modules.limit: The 50 benchmark families do not provide a single common metric or a matched human–LLM comparison for psychology-specific extraction.
modules.name: Assess the complete extraction product

modules.purpose: Enable another researcher to reconstruct consequential decisions and assess where the process could be checked, corrected or redirected.
modules.record: Link final values to source locations, actors, transformations and accepted or rejected alternatives; preserve versioned instructions, exposure timing, adjudication and uncertainty records.
modules.evaluate: Examine whether sources and decision paths can actually be reconstructed, whether uncertainties remain visible and whether correction or escalation was possible. Evaluate final accuracy separately.
modules.question: What records and interfaces enable useful assessment and steering of the process, and which omissions prevent an independent audit?
modules.limit: No benchmark in the selected collection validates complete workflow auditability. Citation and structured-extraction tasks supply partial diagnostics only.
modules.name: Retain an auditable extraction record

position.text: Evaluate the accuracy of the extraction product and the auditability of the process using the same criteria for human, LLM and human–AI workflows.

The original study compared LLM outputs with existing human-extracted review data. Agreement with that reference does not independently establish the quality of the human judgments or a general accuracy ranking between humans and LLMs. Disagreements require source-based investigation.
position.anchor: Introduction; human reference data; discussion of Macnamara

position.text: Do not assume that LLMs are substantially less accurate than human experts or research assistants on the target task. Compare their performance, errors and complementarities empirically, by workflow step and under documented conditions.
position.anchor: Human reference data; discussion of Macnamara; Discussion

position.text: The 50 selected benchmark families concern component capabilities and related extraction tasks. They do not constitute a psychology-specific extraction benchmark, a pooled estimate of progress, or validation of a complete workflow.
Keep model capability, the harness or tools, and the human interaction design distinguishable when comparing workflows. Record which information and assistance became available at each decision.

Auditability makes it possible to assess and steer the quality of each extraction step. A traceable decision may still be wrong; final accuracy and process auditability therefore remain separate outcomes.

The workflow modules below are candidate components and research questions. Their order, allocation to actors, independence requirements and verification intensity require empirical comparison rather than endorsement of a universally validated workflow.
position.anchor: Developing a Human–AI Workflow; practical reporting

position.text: Protocol reproducibility, human–AI interaction, adjudication and complete audit trails extend beyond the component capabilities represented by Challenges A–D. Missing benchmark coverage remains an evidence gap.
